question: The protection of the health, safety and dignity of workers is a fundamental principle of the Union acquis. Article 153 TFEU establishes the Union competence for health and safety at work, while Articles 5 and 6 of Directive 89/391/EEC set out the employer’s responsibility for safety and the prevention and assessment of occupational risks.

Article 31 of the Charter of Fundamental Rights enshrines safe and healthy working conditions, while Principle 10 of the European Pillar of Social Rights reaffirms the right to a high level of protection. The EU strategic framework 2021-2027 and the 2025 guidelines of the European social partners, supported by EU-OSHA, address third-party violence. In view of the above, can the Commission answer the following: 1.

What information does it have on the extent of attacks and incidents of violence against workers in the Member States – and in Greece specifically – and what measures are being taken to prevent and respond to them?

To what extent is the implementation of Articles 5 and 6 of Directive 89/391/EEC ensured with regard to the prevention and assessment of risks arising from attacks or violent behaviours towards workers?

Does it intend to strengthen the implementation of the 2025 guidelines and promote a common European framework for recording, preventing and protecting workers from incidents of violence in the exercise of their duties?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.11.2026) 1.

A series of EU-level surveys and data collections, including the occupational safety and health (OSH) Pulse Worker Survey1, the European Working Conditions Survey2, the European Survey of Enterprises on New and Emerging Risks (ESENER)3 and the European Statistics on Accidents at Work (ESAW)4 data collection, provide information on various aspects related to the extent of attacks and incidents of violence against workers in Member States (including Greece) and the measures taken to address them5.

2. Pursuant to Directive 89/391/EEC6, employers have a duty to ensure the safety and health of workers in every aspect related to work and, within the context of their responsibilities, must take the measures necessary for the safety and health protection of workers. This concerns all occupational risks, including psychosocial risks and risks of attacks and incidents of violence against workers at work.

Member States must transpose EU directives into national legislation, and it is the competent national authorities that are primarily responsible for enforcing national provisions, transposing EU directives and for dealing with issues related to compliance with EU law in concrete individual cases. 3.

As part of the envisaged Quality Jobs Act, the Commission is looking at the need to update OSH protection of workers for modern workplaces, and to further address psychosocial risks at work, among others.

5 For example, according to the European Agency’s for Safety and Health at Work (EU-OSHA), ‘OSH Pulse 2025: Occupational safety and health in the era of climate and digital change’, 16% of EU workers reported having been exposed to violence or verbal abuse in 2025, rising to 25% in health and social care and 22% in education (https://osha.europa.

eu/sites/default/files/documents/OSH-pulse-2025-climate-digitalchange_EN.pdf); according to the Eurofound’s European Working Conditions Survey 2024, 11% of EU workers reported having experienced verbal abuse in the preceding month, 5% threats in the same period, and 2% physical violence in the preceding 12 months (https://www.eurofound.europa.

eu/en/publications/all/europeanworking-conditions-survey-2024-overview-report); in 2024, Eurostat reported 139 fatal and 121 484 non-fatal work accidents involving ‘shock, fright, violence, aggressions, threat and presence’. See https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/databrowser/bookmark/a1a56ecd-bda0-46a8-a69c4e8e90c08c7c?

lang=en&createdAt=2026-10-23T13:20:01Z for related data, and the ESAW Summary methodology 2013, page 28, https://ec.europa.eu/eurostat/documents/3859598/5926181/KS-RA-12-102EN.PDF/56cd35ba-1e8a-4af3-9f9a-b3c47611ff1c?t=1746518538582. The EU-OSHA’s ESENER survey provides information on the way health and safety risks, including related to violence and harassment, are managed at workplaces.

6 Council Directive 89/391/EEC of 12 June 1989 on the introduction of measures to encourage improvements in the safety and health of workers at work, https://eur-lex.europa.eu/legalcontent/EN/TXT/?uri=CELEX%3A01989L0391-20081211&qid=1792756243825.
